headline: Too many parallel sessions, one reviewer: re-charted to three public tracks.
approach: By mid-November about a dozen Claude sessions were building at once across five repos. They produced work faster than one person could review it: 18 open pull requests, more than 40 overdue items and a habit of approving without reading. Each session was sensible; together they had lost the plot.

The re-plan treats review attention as the constraint (Goldratt's Theory of Constraints) and sizes the work to it. At most two Claude sessions run at once, each names its track and milestone before it starts, and anything new gets a date on or after 5 January.

Three tracks are public below. A fourth runs privately and isn't shown here. Nothing was deleted: work that doesn't fit before January is frozen with an owner and one review date, and privacy items are sequenced first, never dropped.

principles.title: Two sessions, maximum
principles.text: One track per session; a session that can't name its milestone doesn't start.

principles.title: Finish before widening
principles.text: Land what is in flight, then freeze. New lanes, sources and features queue for 5 January.

principles.title: Privacy first
principles.text: Open exposures close before any graph work resumes.

principles.title: One weekly review
principles.text: Fridays, 30 minutes: numbers against their baselines, health, re-date or cancel anything overdue, one edit per page.

tracks.role: the build: a public, pre-registered eval suite, published 15 December
the voice: events into checked posts and follow-ups, about two a week
the platform: privacy first, land the graph, then hold steady to January
